recipes.name: Aligot
recipes.description: Stretchy potato pur?e beaten with fresh cheese, garlic and cream.
ingredients: 250 g tome fra?che or young tomme, thinly sliced
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, 18?22 minutes. Drain and rice or mash smooth.
Return potatoes to low heat; beat in butter, garlic and warm milk gradually until creamy.
Add cheese by handfuls, stirring firmly in one direction until melted and stretchy. Season and serve hot.
recipes.sides: Serve with grilled sausage, roast vegetables or a crisp green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Young Cantal or tomme melts well; low-moisture mozzarella gives stretch but a milder flavour.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Blanquette de veau
recipes.description: Veal gently poached with aromatics and finished in a pale cream sauce.
ingredients: 150 ml single cream and 1 tbsp lemon
instructions: Cover veal with cold water; bring just to a simmer and skim. Add onion, carrot, celery and herbs.
Part-cover and simmer gently until tender, 75?90 minutes; add mushrooms for final 15 minutes. Reserve 500 ml broth.
Make a roux with butter and flour; whisk in broth and simmer until lightly thickened. Stir in cream and lemon, return meat and mushrooms, heat without boiling.
recipes.sides: Serve over rice or buttered noodles, with peas or green beans.
recipes.substitutions: Use boneless chicken thighs instead of veal and simmer until cooked through; the broth will be lighter.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: B?uf bourguignon
recipes.description: A slow braise of beef, red wine, mushrooms and aromatic vegetables.
ingredients: 500 ml dry red wine and 300 ml beef stock
instructions: Pat beef dry. Brown lardons, then brown beef in batches in the same casserole; set aside.
Soften onion and carrots; return meat, stir through flour, then add wine and stock while scraping the base. Add garlic and herbs.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2? hours. Brown mushrooms separately, add for final 20 minutes and cook until beef is fork-tender.
recipes.sides: Serve with mashed potatoes, buttered noodles or crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Use beef chuck or shin. For an alcohol-free braise use extra stock with 1 tsp red-wine vinegar.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Bouillabaisse
recipes.description: Tomato, fennel and saffron fish stew inspired by Marseille home cooking.
ingredients: 700 g firm white fish, boneless chunks
1 onion and 1 small fennel bulb, sliced
2 tbsp olive oil and 2 garlic cloves
Pinch saffron, strip orange zest and bay
instructions: Soften onion and fennel in oil for 8 minutes. Add garlic and tomatoes; cook until pulpy.
Add stock, saffron, orange zest and bay. Simmer 15 minutes; remove zest and bay.
Add fish by thickness and simmer gently 5?8 minutes until opaque and flaky. Season, add parsley and serve.
recipes.sides: Serve with toasted bread and garlic rouille or a plain green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Choose any sustainably sourced firm white fish. A little extra fennel can replace saffron aroma, though not its colour.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate for up to 1 day and reheat once until piping hot.
recipes.safety: Keep fish chilled until cooking. Cook until opaque and flaky; avoid cross-contamination from raw seafood.

recipes.name: Brandade de morue
recipes.description: Salt cod worked with olive oil and potato into a warm, soft pur?e.
ingredients: 1 tbsp lemon juice and black pepper
instructions: If starting with salted cod, soak covered in the refrigerator 24?36 hours, changing water several times.
Boil potatoes until tender. Poach cod gently 8?10 minutes, drain and check carefully for bones.
Mash potatoes; flake in fish and beat in warm milk, olive oil and garlic. Season with lemon and pepper.
recipes.sides: Serve with toast, steamed greens or a tomato salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use another firm white fish if salt cod is unavailable; season carefully because it lacks the characteristic cured saltiness.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly for up to 1 day and reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Desalt fish in the refrigerator, changing water regularly; never soak at room temperature. Check carefully for bones and keep raw fish separate from ready-to-eat food.

recipes.name: Cassoulet
recipes.description: Slow-baked white beans with pork and sausage for a hearty casserole.
ingredients: 500 g dried haricot beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Boil soaked beans briskly for 10 minutes, drain, then simmer in fresh water until nearly tender, 35?50 minutes.
Brown pork, sausage and lardons in casserole. Soften onion and carrots; stir in garlic.
Add beans, bay and stock. Cover and bake at 160?C conventional / 140?C fan for 90 minutes, adding hot water if needed; uncover for the final 20 minutes.
recipes.sides: Serve with crusty bread and a sharp green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use about three drained 400 g cans of white beans; reduce oven time to 45–60 minutes.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Cr?pes
recipes.description: Thin pan-cooked pancakes for a simple sweet breakfast or dessert.
instructions: Whisk flour, salt and optional sugar. Beat in eggs, then gradually whisk in milk until smooth; stir in melted butter.
Rest batter for 20 minutes if possible. Heat lightly buttered 20 cm pan over medium heat.
Pour a small ladle and swirl thinly. Cook until edge lifts, flip and briefly cook the other side. Repeat.
recipes.sides: Fill with lemon and sugar, jam, fresh fruit or a savoury filling.
recipes.substitutions: For savoury crêpes omit sugar; replace up to half the flour with buckwheat for a nuttier taste.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Galette compl?te
recipes.description: Buckwheat cr?pe folded around egg, ham and melting cheese.
instructions: Whisk flour, salt, batter egg and water until smooth; rest 20 minutes.
Butter a wide pan, spread a thin layer of batter and cook until top looks dry; flip briefly.
Lower heat, add ham, cheese and an egg. Fold edges inward, cover until white sets and cheese melts.
recipes.sides: Serve with a green salad and unsweetened cider or sparkling water.
recipes.substitutions: Emmental or Comté can replace Gruyère. Use cooked turkey instead of ham if preferred.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Cook the filling egg until the white is completely set; use pasteurised eggs for vulnerable diners.

recipes.name: Choucroute garnie
recipes.description: Fermented cabbage slowly cooked with apple, wine, smoked meats and potatoes.
ingredients: 250 ml dry white wine and 250 ml water
instructions: Soften onion in oil, add apple and sauerkraut and toss.
Add wine, water, bay and juniper. Cover and simmer gently for 60 minutes. Boil potatoes separately until tender.
Add sausage and cooked pork for the final 20 minutes until piping hot. Serve with cabbage and potatoes; remove whole spices.
recipes.sides: Serve with Dijon mustard and crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Replace wine with unsalted stock or apple juice plus a splash of vinegar. Rinse sauerkraut for a milder result.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Clafoutis
recipes.description: Baked custard-like batter surrounds pitted cherries for an easy dessert.
instructions: Heat oven to 180?C conventional / 160?C fan. Butter a 23 cm dish and arrange pitted cherries.
Whisk eggs and sugar; beat in flour, then gradually whisk in milk and vanilla until smooth.
Pour over cherries and bake 35?40 minutes until puffed, golden and set in centre.
recipes.sides: Serve warm or at room temperature with crème fraîche or plain yoghurt.
recipes.substitutions: Use pitted plums or apricots instead of cherries and bake until the centre is set.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Coq au vin
recipes.description: Chicken braised slowly with red wine, mushrooms and onions.
ingredients: 400 ml dry red wine and 250 ml chicken stock
200 g mushrooms and 150 g pearl onions
instructions: Brown lardons, then chicken in batches; set aside. Soften onion and carrots in the casserole.
Stir in flour, then gradually wine and stock, scraping the base. Add garlic, herbs and lardons.
Return chicken, cover and simmer 60 minutes. Add browned mushrooms and onions; simmer uncovered 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
recipes.sides: Serve with mash, buttered noodles or crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: For an alcohol-free version use chicken stock with 1 tbsp red-wine vinegar instead of wine.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Cook chicken to at least 75°C at the thickest part, away from bone. Keep raw poultry separate from other ingredients.

recipes.name: Croque monsieur
recipes.description: Toasted ham and cheese sandwich with a quick b?chamel browned on top.
instructions: Heat grill to medium-high. Melt butter, stir in flour 1 minute, then whisk in milk until smooth and thick; season with nutmeg.
Spread mustard on bread, add ham and half the cheese, close sandwiches and place on tray.
Top with b?chamel and remaining cheese; grill 4?6 minutes until golden and hot throughout.
recipes.sides: Serve with a dressed green salad or tomato soup.
recipes.substitutions: Emmental or mature Swiss-style cheese melts well in place of Gruyère; omit mustard for a milder sandwich.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Gratin dauphinois
recipes.description: Thin potato slices bake slowly in seasoned cream until tender and golden.
instructions: Heat oven to 170?C conventional / 150?C fan. Rub baking dish with cut garlic, then butter it.
Slice potatoes thinly and evenly; layer in dish, seasoning between layers.
Warm milk and cream until steaming, pour over potatoes and bake uncovered 70?80 minutes until tender and golden.
recipes.sides: Serve with roast chicken and green vegetables.
recipes.substitutions: Use semi-skimmed milk for a lighter result; add a little grated cheese on top as a variation.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Hachis parmentier
recipes.description: Seasoned minced beef under a layer of buttery mashed potato.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, drain and mash with butter and warm milk.
Soften onion in oil; add beef and carrot and cook until browned throughout. Add stock and thyme; simmer until most liquid evaporates.
Spoon beef into dish, cover with mash and optional cheese. Bake at 200?C / 180?C fan for 20?25 minutes until golden.
recipes.sides: Serve with green beans or a dressed salad.
recipes.substitutions: Finely chop leftover cooked pot-au-feu beef instead of mince and moisten with stock.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Quiche Lorraine
recipes.description: A savoury custard tart with smoked lardons in a crisp pastry shell.
instructions: Heat oven to 190?C / 170?C fan. Line a 23 cm tin, prick pastry and chill 10 minutes. Blind bake 15 minutes; remove weights and bake 5 minutes more.
Cook lardons until lightly golden and drain. Whisk eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and pepper.
Scatter lardons in pastry, pour in custard and bake 30?35 minutes until just set. Rest 10 minutes.
recipes.sides: Serve warm or cold with a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Add 75 g Gruyère as a common variation; use milk in place of some cream for a lighter custard.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Tarte flamb?e (flammekueche)
recipes.description: Thin flatbread topped with cr?me fra?che, onions and lardons, baked hot and fast.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil and ? tsp salt
100 g fromage blanc or thick yoghurt
instructions: Mix flour, water, oil and salt into smooth dough. Knead briefly, cover and rest 20 minutes.
Heat oven to 250?C / 230?C fan with a heavy tray inside. Mix cr?me fra?che and fromage blanc with pepper and nutmeg.
Roll dough very thin, spread with cream, add onion and lardons. Bake 10?14 minutes until crisp and toppings cooked.
recipes.sides: Serve hot with a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use sour cream loosened with a spoonful of plain yoghurt if fromage blanc is unavailable.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Tartiflette
recipes.description: Potatoes, onions and lardons baked beneath melting Reblochon cheese.
instructions: Boil potatoes until just tender, 15?20 minutes; drain, cool slightly and slice.
Brown lardons, add onion and cook soft. Pour in wine or stock and simmer 2 minutes.
Layer potatoes and onion mixture in dish. Set Reblochon rind-side up on top and bake at 200?C / 180?C fan for 25?30 minutes.
recipes.sides: Serve with green salad and cornichons to balance the rich cheese.
recipes.substitutions: A ripe Camembert can replace Reblochon, though the flavour will differ.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Pot-au-feu
recipes.description: Beef and root vegetables slowly simmer into a simple restorative broth.
instructions: Put beef in pot, cover with cold water and bring slowly to simmer; skim foam.
Add onion studded with cloves, bay and peppercorns. Part-cover and simmer gently for 2 hours.
Add carrots, leeks, turnips and celery; simmer 35?45 minutes until beef and vegetables are tender. Slice meat across grain and serve with broth.
recipes.sides: Serve with mustard, horseradish, cornichons and crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Beef shin, brisket or chuck all work; simmer until fork-tender because cut and size change cooking time.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Ratatouille
recipes.description: A slow-cooked mixture of aubergine, courgette, peppers and tomatoes with herbs.
instructions: Salt aubergine lightly for 15 minutes and pat dry. Brown in batches in half the oil; set aside.
Cook courgettes and peppers in remaining oil until coloured, then soften onion. Add garlic, tomatoes and herbs.
Return aubergine, cover and simmer gently 30?35 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season and fold in basil.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread, rice or roast chicken; leftovers are good with eggs.
recipes.substitutions: Use any mix of aubergine, courgette and peppers in similar quantities; add tomatoes to keep the stew moist.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Salade ni?oise
recipes.description: Composed salad of tuna, egg, potatoes and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, lemon and Dijon
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender. Add green beans for final 4 minutes; drain and cool. Boil eggs 8?9 minutes, cool and halve.
Whisk oil, lemon and mustard with salt and pepper. Arrange lettuce, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, tuna, eggs and olives.
Drizzle dressing and add anchovies if using. Serve promptly.
recipes.sides: Serve with crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Replace tuna with cooked salmon or chickpeas; omit anchovies for a milder salad.
recipes.storage: Keep components chilled and assemble just before serving. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 1 day.
recipes.safety: Use fully cooked eggs. Keep tuna chilled after opening and do not leave the assembled salad at room temperature.

recipes.name: Soupe ? l?oignon gratin?e
recipes.description: Long-cooked onions and stock topped with toasted bread and melted cheese.
ingredients: 30 g butter and 1 tbsp olive oil
instructions: Cook onions in butter and oil on low, stirring often, 35?45 minutes until deep golden.
Stir in flour for 1 minute. Gradually add stock and thyme; simmer 15 minutes and season.
Toast bread. Ladle soup into grill-safe bowls, top with toast and cheese, grill until bubbling and golden.
recipes.sides: Serve with a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetable stock for a vegetarian version; choose cheese made with suitable rennet if needed.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Poulet basquaise
recipes.description: Chicken simmers with peppers, tomatoes and gentle paprika-chilli seasoning.
instructions: Brown chicken in oil on both sides; remove. Cook onion and peppers in the pot for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and paprika, stir briefly, then add tomatoes and stock. Return chicken skin-side up.
Cover and simmer 35?40 minutes until cooked through. Uncover briefly to reduce sauce and finish with parsley.
recipes.sides: Serve with rice, potatoes or crusty bread to catch the sauce.
recipes.substitutions: Boneless thighs cook faster; check doneness before reducing the sauce. Omit chilli for a mild version.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Cook chicken to at least 75°C at the thickest part, away from bone. Keep raw poultry and its juices separate.

recipes.name: Pissaladi?re
recipes.description: Onion tart on a soft bread base, topped with anchovies and olives.
ingredients: 7 g instant yeast and 180 ml warm water
1 tbsp olive oil and ? tsp salt
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, water, oil and salt into dough. Knead briefly, cover and rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Cook onions with oil and thyme on low 25?30 minutes until very soft; cool. Heat oven to 220?C / 200?C fan.
Roll dough to an oval, spread with onions, arrange anchovies and olives, then bake 18?22 minutes until base is golden.
recipes.sides: Serve warm or at room temperature with a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use capers instead of anchovies for a vegetarian topping and add salt sparingly.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Moules marini?res
recipes.description: Mussels steam in shallot, parsley and white-wine broth for a simple shared meal.
ingredients: 150 ml dry white wine and 100 ml water
instructions: Scrub mussels under running water and remove beards. Discard cracked ones and open mussels that do not close when tapped.
Soften shallots in butter 3 minutes. Add wine and water and bring to boil.
Add mussels, cover and steam 4?6 minutes, shaking pot once. Discard any that remain closed; add parsley and serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with chips, crusty bread or a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use fish stock and lemon instead of wine. Do not substitute frozen mussels in the steaming method.
recipes.storage: Best eaten immediately; do not keep cooked mussels for later.
recipes.safety: Buy live mussels from a reputable supplier, keep chilled and cook the day of purchase. Discard cracked mussels and any that do not close before cooking; after steaming discard any that remain closed.

recipes.name: Madeleines
recipes.description: Small shell-shaped sponge cakes scented with lemon; chilling the batter helps texture.
instructions: Melt butter and cool. Whisk eggs and sugar until pale and thick; fold in sifted flour, baking powder, salt and zest.
Fold in melted butter, cover and refrigerate batter at least 1 hour. Heat oven to 200?C / 180?C fan.
Butter and flour madeleine tin, fill each shell three-quarters and bake 9?12 minutes until risen and golden. Cool on rack.
recipes.sides: Serve with tea, coffee or fresh fruit.
recipes.substitutions: Use orange zest or a few drops of vanilla instead of lemon zest.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Tarte Tatin
recipes.description: Apples caramelise beneath pastry and are turned out for a glossy fruit topping.
ingredients: 6 firm apples, peeled, cored and quartered
1 tbsp lemon juice and pinch salt
instructions: Heat oven to 200?C / 180?C fan. In oven-safe 22 cm pan melt sugar to amber; carefully whisk in butter and salt.
Arrange lemon-tossed apples tightly in caramel. Cook gently 8?10 minutes until beginning to soften.
Lay pastry over apples and tuck edges in. Bake 25?30 minutes until deeply golden. Rest 5 minutes, then carefully invert onto plate.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with crème fraîche or vanilla ice cream.
recipes.substitutions: Firm pears can replace apples; cook until beginning to soften before covering with pastry.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: ?ufs en meurette
recipes.description: Poached eggs over toasted bread with a red-wine sauce, mushrooms and lardons.
ingredients: 300 ml red wine and 250 ml beef stock
instructions: Brown lardons; add onion and mushrooms and cook soft. Stir in flour, then gradually whisk in wine and stock.
Add bay and simmer 20?25 minutes until lightly thickened; remove bay.
Poach eggs in gently simmering water for 3?4 minutes until whites set. Spoon sauce over toast, top with egg and parsley.
recipes.sides: Serve over toasted bread with a green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use vegetable stock and omit lardons for a meat-free sauce; cook egg yolks fully if needed.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Use fresh or pasteurised eggs. Cook whites fully; avoid serving runny eggs to vulnerable people.

recipes.name: Endives au jambon
recipes.description: Endives wrapped in ham bake under a simple cheese sauce, balancing their gentle bitterness.
instructions: Simmer endives in lightly salted water 15?20 minutes until tender. Drain well and gently squeeze out excess liquid.
Make b?chamel: melt butter, stir in flour, then gradually whisk in milk; simmer until thick and season.
Wrap endives in ham in baking dish, cover with sauce and cheese. Bake at 200?C / 180?C fan for 20?25 minutes until bubbling.
recipes.sides: Serve with boiled potatoes or crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Add a teaspoon of Dijon mustard to the sauce or replace Gruyère with Emmental.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Far breton
recipes.description: Dense baked custard cake often made with prunes, sliced after cooling.
instructions: Heat oven to 180?C / 160?C fan. Butter a 23 cm dish and scatter prunes over base.
Whisk eggs and sugar; whisk in flour and salt, then gradually milk, butter and vanilla until smooth.
Pour over prunes and bake 45?55 minutes until puffed, golden and set in centre. Cool in dish before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve plain with tea or a spoon of yoghurt.
recipes.substitutions: Use raisins or chopped dried apricots instead of prunes; reduce sugar slightly if fruit is sweet.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.

recipes.name: Piperade
recipes.description: Peppers, tomatoes and onion cook down with paprika and Espelette-style chilli.
instructions: Cook onion and peppers in oil over medium-low heat for 12?15 minutes until soft.
Add garlic, paprika and chilli; stir briefly, then add tomatoes. Simmer uncovered 15?20 minutes until thick.
Season. For egg variation make wells, add eggs, cover and cook until whites are set; scatter parsley if available.
recipes.sides: Serve with bread, rice or grilled chicken.
recipes.substitutions: Use piment d’Espelette if available; sweet paprika with a pinch of chilli is a practical alternative.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours. Keep for up to 2 days for fish and shellfish dishes or up to 3 days for other dishes; reheat once until steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Keep raw meat and seafood separate from ready-to-eat food. Cook poultry thoroughly and fish until opaque and flaky. Chill leftovers promptly; discard food left at room temperature for over 2 hours.
